extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners handling reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examining and prosecuting ex parte patent reexamination proceedings, including how to treat prior art, admissions, claim construction, 35 U.S.C. 112 issues, new matter, scope-enlargement, and the use of previously cited/considered art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of patent-owner admissions as prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: An admission by the patent owner (from the patent, file history, litigation, or presented during reexamination) is part of the scope and content of the prior art and may be used in reexamination as evidence of prior art and obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admissions are acknowledged facts and require no independent proof. The scope/content of an admission may need to be determined from the record or file history. The examiner must not ignore admissions by the patent owner and should use them in conjunction with patents and printed publications to determine prior art (citing Seiko, Kimbell, McGaughey).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on third-party submissions of admissions
rubrics_metrics.description: A third party may not submit admissions of the patent owner made outside the record as part of a reexamination request
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such submissions would be outside the scope of reexamination; only admissions of record (in the patent file or presented in the proceeding or litigation) are proper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim interpretation in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Original patent claims in reexamination are given the broadest reasonable interpretation consistent with the specification; limitations in the specification are not read into the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: for reexamination of expired patents whose claims cannot be amended, apply a policy of narrow construction favoring validity (see In re Papst-Motoren). The statutory presumption of validity (35 U.S.C. 282) does not apply in reexamination (In re Etter).

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 112 compliance limited to amendatory/new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: When new claims are presented or any part of the disclosure is amended, compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112 (enablement/ written description and claim definiteness) is to be examined only as to the amendatory (new) matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not raise 112 issues as to matter that is identical to the original patent disclosure. If an amendment adds a limitation not found in the original claim/disclosure, the examiner should consider 112 only with respect to that limitation. See MPEP §§ 2163 - 2173.05(v).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on new matter (35 U.S.C. 132) in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 305 authorizes examination under 35 U.S.C. 132 which prohibits introduction of new matter into the disclosure during reexamination; new matter added to claims or affecting claim limitations should lead to rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112 (written description).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the relationship between the written description requirement and the new matter prohibition (see MPEP § 2163.06).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of the specification must comply with 35 U.S.C. 112
rubrics_metrics.description: If the specification is amended in reexamination, the examiner must ensure the amendment meets 35 U.S.C. 112 requirements because an amendment can redefine claim terms and render claims unsupported or unclear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment to the specification can cause claims to fail 112 even if claims themselves were not amended.

rubrics_metrics.name: No enlargement of claim scope (35 U.S.C. 305)
rubrics_metrics.description: No proposed amended or new claim enlarging the scope of the claims of the patent will be permitted in a reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine new/amended claims under 35 U.S.C. 305 to determine enlargement. If a claim enlarges scope it must be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 305 using form paragraph 22.11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for determining enlargement of scope
rubrics_metrics.description: A presented claim 'enlarges the scope' where it is broader than each and every claim of the patent; a claim is broadened if it contains any conceivable product or process that would not have infringed the original patent, and it is broadened if broader in any one respect even if narrower in others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 1412.03 for guidance on what is broadening. Examiner should identify and explain the claim limitations that broaden the scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 22.11 for 35 U.S.C. 305 rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Use form paragraph 22.11 to reject claims under 35 U.S.C. 305 as enlarging the scope of the patent in ex parte reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 2 identify the claim limitations considered to broaden the claim and explain in the Office action why those limitations broaden the scope (see MPEP § 2258 guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify claims subject to prior Office or court decision
rubrics_metrics.description: If some patent claims have been the subject of a prior Office or court decision, those claims not subject to reexamination should be identified and handled according to the relevant MPEP sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 2242 and 2286; where other proceedings are copending, see MPEP §§ 2282-2286. For a 'live' claim dependent on a claim not subject to reexamination, see MPEP § 2260.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: All 'live' claims are reexamined
rubrics_metrics.description: All existing claims not held invalid by a final decision (i.e., 'live' claims) in the patent will be reexamined; the reexamination certificate will indicate the status of all patent claims and any added patentable claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction requirements are improper in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction requirements cannot be made in a reexamination proceeding because no statutory basis for restriction exists in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ancillary amendments permissible to correct matters incident to patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments necessary and incident to patentability (e.g., correcting an inadvertent failure to claim foreign priority or clarifying continuing status) may be made during reexamination if necessary to overcome a reference applied against a claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming foreign and domestic priority in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner may perfect previously made foreign priority claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) by submitting certified copies; in some circumstances patent owner may submit both the priority claim and certified copy for the first time in reexamination but certain limitations apply for patents matured from applications filed on/after November 29, 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If correcting or adding a priority claim for a patent matured from a utility/plant application filed on/after Nov 29, 2000, the patent owner must file a grantable petition for an unintentionally delayed priority claim under 37 CFR 1.55(c) or 1.78(a)(3) as appropriate. Reexamination cannot be used to add or correct benefit claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) after a patent has issued for patents matured from applications filed on/after Nov 29, 2000 (AIPA amendment). See MPEP §§ 201.11, 201.14(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: No renewal required for previously made priority/benefit claims
rubrics_metrics.description: No renewal of previously made claims for foreign priority under 35 U.S.C. 119 or domestic benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) or 120 is necessary during reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Correction of inventorship may be made during reexamination (see 37 CFR 1.324 and MPEP § 1481); if a petition under 37 CFR 1.324 is granted, the reexamination certificate will reflect the change of inventorship (merging the Certificate of Correction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of affidavits in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits under 37 CFR 1.131 and 1.132 may be utilized in reexamination, but an affidavit under 37 CFR 1.131 may not be used to 'swear back' of a reference patent if that reference patent claims the 'same invention' as the patent under reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 1.131 cannot be used to overcome a reference patent claiming the same invention, consider an affidavit under 37 CFR 1.130 (see MPEP § 718) or raising the issue via an appropriate reissue application (see MPEP § 1449.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Issues not within scope of reexamination (e.g., public use/on sale/fraud)
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions other than those based on patents or printed publications (for example public use, on sale, fraud, abandonment, 35 U.S.C. 102(c), etc.) raised by the third-party requester or patent owner will be noted but not considered in reexamination; form paragraph 22.03 should be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such issues are raised by the patent owner or requester, identify the issues in bracket 1 of form paragraph 22.03 and advise the patentee that filing a reissue application may be desirable to have those issues considered. Examiners should not independently raise such issues in reexamination. If the examiner independently discovers such questions not raised by the requester or patent owner, they will not be noted in Office actions (37 CFR 1.552(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for reexamination filed on a patent after it has been reissued
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination requests filed on a patent after it has been reissued will be denied because the prior patent has been surrendered; to reexamine the reissued patent, a new request based on the reissue specification and claims must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any patent-owner amendments accompanying the initial reexamination request should treat the granted reissue text as the patent text; bracketing/underlining should reflect the reissue changes. See MPEP § 2285 for post-issuance reissue timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner must check prior file history before using previously cited/considered art ('old art')
rubrics_metrics.description: Before making a rejection in reexamination, the examiner must ascertain whether the art forming the basis of the rejection was previously cited/considered in an earlier concluded Office examination (referred to as 'old art').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the rejection is based on a combination of old art and newly cited art, the rejection is proper (see In re Hiniker). If old art alone is the sole basis, different rules apply depending on whether reexamination was ordered on or after Nov 2, 2002.

rubrics_metrics.name: Old art as sole basis for SNQ — reexamination ordered on/after Nov 2, 2002
rubrics_metrics.description: For reexaminations ordered on or after Nov 2, 2002, reliance solely on old art does not necessarily preclude a substantial new question of patentability (SNQ); determinations are fact-specific and an old-art-only SNQ may exist where old art is presented/viewed in a new light or with a material new argument/interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an Office action first sets forth an SNQ based solely on old art, include form paragraph 22.01.01 identifying the old art and explaining how it raises an SNQ (the first time old art is applied in the proceeding). Form paragraph instructions: bracket 2 insert the old art basis; bracket 3 explain how/why it applies (e.g., new light, new argument). This form paragraph is used only the first time the old art is applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Old art as sole basis — reexamination ordered prior to Nov 2, 2002 (Portola Packaging guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: For reexaminations ordered prior to Nov 2, 2002, old art generally cannot be used as the sole basis for rejection (subject to specific exceptions); the Portola Packaging decision controls and the Office must follow prescribed procedures to determine whether prosecution must be terminated or rejections withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures include: (a) ascertain the order date; (b) determine for prior related proceeding what prior art was relied upon to reject or was cited and discussed; (c) base rejections at least in part on art not previously relied upon or discussed; (d) withdraw rejections based only on previously relied/cited-and-discussed art; (e) terminate prosecution where only remaining rejections are entirely based on such old art. The Director may search for new art before terminating reexamination. Unusual fact patterns should be referred to the Technology Center (TC) Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples and exceptions where old art may be relied upon despite prior citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrative unusual fact patterns where previously cited art may nonetheless support reexamination include: (a) the old art is presented in a new light or different way due to a material new argument; (b) only part of a cited reference (e.g., portion of a textbook) was previously considered and other portions now relied upon teach the claims; (c) prior examiner misappreciated the reference (wrong date, inadequate antedating declaration, incorrect filing date); (d) a foreign-language reference was not previously fully/accurately translated; (e) cumulative references that merely reiterate verbatim teachings of previously applied references are generally not grounds alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These examples are illustrative, not exhaustive. Where a foreign language reference is now fully translated and the translation shows teachings that were not previously considered, reexamination may proceed. Cumulative references that substantially reiterate prior teachings will rarely preclude reliance on new art because most references add new information or present it differently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices for Portola Packaging compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If prosecution is terminated under Portola Packaging or a rejection is withdrawn to comply with Portola, specific notice language should be used in the Notice of Intent to Issue a reexamination certificate or in Office actions withdrawing rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (a) Termination notice: indicate prosecution terminated based on In re Portola Packaging and that no patentability determination has been made; (b) Withdrawal notice: state that the rejection(s) based on [identify art] is/are withdrawn in view of In re Portola Packaging and that no patentability determination in view of such prior art has been made.
